title: Horizontal pasting of canonical duality mates on the iterated pullback
statement: Let f:X→Y be qcqs, g:Y′→Y and h:Z→Y′ morphisms with Y,Y′,Z qcqs, and fix derived module categories in one universe [def-pc-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let X′=X×_Y Y′, P=X′×_{Y′} Z, Q=X×_Y Z [def-pc-fibre-product], and let e:P≅Q be canonical pullback associativity. Choose a,a′,d,c right adjoints to the lifted derived direct images for X→Y, X′→Y′, P→Z, Q→Z, with supplied adjunctions [lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint]. Assume ordinary derived base change for (f,g), (X′→Y′,h), and (f,h≫g) is invertible on every quasi-coherent input [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. For K∈D_QCoh(Y), let μ,ν,λ be their respective canonical duality mates [def-sc-duality-equation-base-change-map], with ν evaluated at Lg* K. Then the arrow L(pr₁:P→X′)*μ ≫ ν is isomorphic in Arrow(D(O_P)) to L(e.hom)*λ. Neither μ nor ν nor λ is assumed invertible. No open subschemes, restriction functors, or supplied isomorphisms q,r,δ occur in this statement.

proof.text: Construct the source and target endpoint isomorphisms explicitly using horizontalMateSourceIso and horizontalMateTargetIso. They use the coherent pullback composition and the direct-image conjugate/right-adjoint uniqueness construction; no inverse of a duality mate is used.

Apply horizontal_duality_mate_commutativity for the fixed endpoint comparisons. Its symmetric equality is the commuting-square hypothesis of Arrow.isoMk. Package the resulting isomorphism in Nonempty.
